rows.32:5f74:
They say plenty of romances get their start thanks to an umbrella.
You know, like in those romance comics for girls.{p}
rows.32:5fd8:
So you don't.
Lots of people are like that, aren't they?{p}
rows.32:6014:
Boys especially.
That's why, in the rainy season, I often see people waiting out the rain by the shoe lockers.{p}
rows.32:6070:
My, how admirable.
But not everyone in the world is like you, are they?
Boys especially. I'd think it's rare for one to keep a spare umbrella at school.
But you know, for a girl, that's also the perfect chance for romance.{p}
rows.32:6140:
Oh, really.
So that's the kind of person you are, {a}.
A man who's a disgrace to the human race.
You can't understand the pain in other people's hearts, can you?
You won't notice it until the same thing happens to you.
I can't forgive people like that.
I can't forgive them.{p}
rows.32:6274:
And you call yourself a journalist?
Do you really think you can get by in the newspaper club without taking an interest in people?
I can't tell my story to someone so careless.
Why don't you answer a little more seriously?
Come on, answer me.{p}I asked what you think of Tsukahara.
rows.32:63e4:
Hmm, is that so.
Well, if that's how you feel, that's fine.
But God does love his little pranks, doesn't he?
After all, he gave Tachibana one more chance.{p}
rows.32:648c:
It was when the rainy season was nearly over.
Maybe Tsukahara was the type who never kept a spare umbrella at school.
He was waiting out the rain again.
All by himself.
And Tachibana had an umbrella with her.
A big blue umbrella.{p}
rows.32:6568:
Tachibana hesitated.
She couldn't just stand by and watch Tsukahara in trouble.
But if she went to him, he might not like it.
In the end, though, she couldn't bear to watch him stuck there any longer, and she rushed out.{p}
rows.32:6640:
"Um... please, use this umbrella."
At first, when he saw her, he looked annoyed, but he soon smiled.
"Oh, thanks a lot.
Want to walk home together?"{p}
rows.32:66dc:
She hadn't meant to walk home with him.
But he pushily pulled her under the umbrella with him anyway.{p}
rows.32:6744:
She felt terribly awkward.
But he just went on talking anyway.
"Man, I'm sorry.
I just haven't had any time lately.
I've been busy, y'know, with this and that.
You get it, right?
I just want to be nice to everybody.
It's not like I'm into anyone or anything.
Right? So it's not like I started hating you, Yukari..."{p}
rows.32:6890:
As he said that, he suddenly tried to kiss her.
"Please stop."
Caught off guard, Tachibana was startled and refused him.
She still loved him, but she already knew he was only playing around with her.
She believed that kissing was wrong unless two people loved each other.
So she shoved Tsukahara away.{p}
rows.32:69e8:
Honestly, he was taken aback.
No girl had ever turned him down before.
At first he tried to laugh it off, but his pride had been badly wounded.
So he went for her.
"Don't you screw with me!"
Tachibana was shocked.
The Tsukahara she'd thought was so kind was coming at her with a monstrous look on his face.{p}
rows.32:6b30:
She swung the umbrella around wildly.
"Stop!
Please stop!"
Suddenly, she felt a dull impact through her hands.
The hands holding the umbrella suddenly grew heavy, as if it had caught on something.
"Gyaaah..."
...Tsukahara was groaning.
When she looked, the tip of the umbrella was stuck in his left eye.{p}
rows.32:6c44:
...Ow!
Just then, a faint pain shot through my eye.
My left eye, too, just like in the story.
Iwashita went on with her story without noticing.{p}
rows.32:6cdc:
"The umbrella was driven in deep.
The blood flowing out of the wound etched a red pattern across the blue umbrella."{p}
rows.32:6d48:
Throb... throb...
What's happening to me?
The pain in my left eye was getting stronger and stronger.
No, this was more than pain.
It was hot.
It felt like it was burning.
What...
What on earth is this?{p}
rows.32:6e20:
"Tsukahara didn't care how he looked anymore.
He pulled the umbrella's tip out of his left eye and tried to lunge at her.
Tachibana was so terrified that she shut her eyes tight and just thrust the umbrella out.
Not knowing what she was doing, she thrust it out again and again and again."{p}
rows.32:6f28:
It hurts!
Searing pain shot through my body, all over.
It felt like something was being stabbed into me.
I crumpled to the floor.
"Heh... Does it hurt?
That's the pain Tsukahara felt."
...I realized Iwashita was smiling down at me.{p}
rows.32:7018:
"I figured it out while we were talking.
You're the same breed as Tsukahara.
If I let you live, some other girl, somewhere, is going to end up crying.
So I'm going to kill you."
...What?
But Iwashita shouldn't have done anything to me.
So why this pain...?
As if she had read my mind, Iwashita bent down over me.{p}
rows.32:7134:
"I've put Tachibana's curse on you...
You'll feel the pain Tsukahara felt, and you'll die the same way he did."
With her eyes slanted up, her smile was not that of the Iwashita I'd seen until now.
It was something more evil.......... like a witch.{p}
rows.32:7204:
"That's right... I'm a witch.
A witch who protects girls from wicked men..."
Iwashita's smile grew wider.
No... that's ridiculous.
But this pain was covering my whole body.
I was slowly losing consciousness.
I don't want to die like this...
I tried to struggle.
But I couldn't even lift a finger anymore.
As I was swallowed up by agony and darkness, Iwashita watched me, delighted..........{p}
rows.32:7364:
That's right.
Tachibana really was a devoted girl.{p}
rows.32:73bc:
That's exactly why she was content just to watch him.
But Tsukahara wasn't willing to leave it at that.
Having her watching him all the time? No way was he going to put up with that.
What a horrible man.
So he gathered together the girls who always hung around him...{p}
rows.32:74ac:
One day, Tachibana was called out by a group of girls.
And they surrounded her.
"We hear you've been following Tsukahara around?"
"Can't you tell you're a pain in his neck?"
...They all laid into Tachibana, one after another.
Poor Tachibana couldn't even talk back.{p}
rows.32:75c8:
Of course she was mortified.
She hadn't done anything wrong, after all.
But to think Tsukahara found her that much of a nuisance.
And that he'd gone and told other people.
Her pride was torn to shreds.
Tachibana went home... and slit her wrists.{p}
rows.32:76c4:
Unfortunately, her family didn't find her in time.
By the time they did, they say she had already stopped breathing.{p}
rows.32:77d0:
If he were right here, {a}, you'd want to punch him too, wouldn't you?
...But you can't.
Because Tsukahara is dead.
And not just dead. Murdered.{p}
rows.32:7870:
By whom, you ask?
Heh heh... Who knows?
He was found dead, stabbed over and over.
And they say there was an umbrella stuck in his body.
A red one, too, exactly like the one Tachibana used to carry.
What do you suppose that means?
Heh heh...
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next, I wonder?{p}
rows.32:7988:
Scary, you say?
You're scared of Tachibana?
All she does is watch from a distance.
It doesn't cause Tsukahara any trouble at all.
What do you mean, scary?{p}Do you think Tachibana is weird?
rows.32:7a70:
Weird? How cruel.
You're someone who doesn't understand true devotion, aren't you?
...Never mind.
No matter how much I tell someone like you about her feelings, it would be pointless.
Let's continue the story.
She meant to go on watching over Tsukahara.
But the god of fate didn't abandon her.{p}
rows.32:7c54:
...Some time after that, Tsukahara found a present in his desk.
Not that that sort of thing was anything unusual for him.{p}
rows.32:7cec:
When he looked inside, it was a folding umbrella.
"Huh. What a lame present."
...He said nasty things like that about it.
And yet, when it started to rain after school, he took that umbrella out.{p}
rows.32:7db8:
"A fan of mine gave it to me 'cause they didn't want me catching a cold."
He didn't forget to brag about that, either.{p}
rows.32:7ed8: Creak... creak... A groaning, creaking sound.{p}
rows.32:7f70:
Tsukahara was completely wrapped up from the chest up.
The students watching burst out laughing.
Tsukahara, always acting so cool, had made a total fool of himself.
But Tsukahara's umbrella didn't open.
Everyone thought he was just embarrassed at being laughed at.{p}
rows.32:8070:
But before long, blood came gushing out from inside the umbrella.
...Someone screamed.{p}
rows.32:80f0:
The teachers rushed over and pulled Tsukahara out of the umbrella.
But by then, they say, everything from his neck up was already gone.
And of course, it wasn't inside the umbrella either.
All those people had been watching, yet no one could tell where Tsukahara's head had vanished to.
The next day, Tachibana quietly disappeared.
They say she transferred to a school in some faraway town.{p}
rows.32:823c:
Not that anyone ever paid any attention to a girl as plain as her.
Heh heh...
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next, I wonder?{p}
